title: Dhaka rickshaw art
summary: Cycle rickshaws in Dhaka, Bangladesh, carry a painted tin panel on the back and a decorated hood. Painters work in glossy enamel, packing the panel with flowers, birds, ripples and stars in hot pinks, yellows and greens, then edge it with tinsel and foil.
howToPlay: Look at the panel plan on the card: each flower, bird or star has its own enamel colour.
Choose an enamel colour, then a motif from the tray.
Touch the panel to paint. The mirror partner on the other side is painted at the same moment.
Press Check to compare your panel with the plan.
rules: The panel is mirrored left to right, so each stroke is painted in up to two places at once.
A place counts only when both its motif and its enamel colour match the plan.
Painting the same motif in the same colour again wipes it off.
Three stars need a near perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Rickshaw painting is a street art of Dhaka, where artists decorate the back panel, the hood and the seat of a cycle rickshaw so that each machine becomes a small gallery in traffic. Birds, blooms and village scenes are favourite subjects.
